strengths: Multiple converging mechanistic techniques (steering, patching, noising, swaps, attention blocking) all support cached retrieval hypothesis with consistent temporal precedence patterns
Rigorous experimental design with appropriate controls (PANL+1 control, same-confidence swaps to isolate confidence-specific effects, trial length matching)

Significant finding that verbal confidence representations explain substantial variance beyond token log-probabilities (R²=0.084 for logprobs alone), providing evidence for second-order evaluation mechanism
Addresses important practically-relevant question about how widely-deployed verbal confidence is generated in LLMs
Results replicate across model architectures (Gemma, Qwen), prompt formats (categorical, numeric), with consistent temporal ordering of effects
Comprehensive methods documentation enabling reproducibility, with full prompts and detailed hyperparameters
Clear presentation with effective visualizations and well-motivated theoretical framing connecting to decision neuroscience literature
weaknesses: Limited model scope (only Gemma 3 27B and Qwen 2.5 7B) without exploration of generalization to frontier models or very small models, limiting claims about generality

Simplified experimental setting with unclear ecological validity: no chain-of-thought reasoning, answer provided in prompt rather than autoregressively generated, and evaluation only on factual QA—impacts transferability of findings
Partial recovery from activation patching (only ~50% at peak layer for PANL) suggests confidence computation is more distributed than single-position hypothesis suggests, weakening causal claims

Attention blocking shows clearer results in minimal numeric prompt but not in realistic categorical prompt, with routing through intermediate tokens masking direct pathways—suggests information flow may be less direct than presented
No demonstration of actionable interventions to improve calibration; findings remain mechanistic without clear practical applications
Moderate model calibration (ECE 0.12-0.06) leaves unclear whether mechanisms apply to well-calibrated systems or if different systems use different strategies
Linear probing captures only linear readouts of representations; nonlinear components not explored despite potential importance
Steering vectors created from only 25 trials with no robustness analysis; corruption calibration set uses only 100 trials without sufficiency justification

strengths: Well-motivated research questions addressing how LLMs generate confidence reports, with clear relevance to model reliability and deployment

Comprehensive experimental design with multiple converging techniques (activation steering, patching, noising, swap, attention blocking) that systematically build evidence for the cached retrieval hypothesis

Thorough generalization testing across three different model architectures (Gemma, Owen, Magistral), multiple datasets (TriviaQA, BigMath, MMLU), and multiple prompt formats (categorical, numeric, reasoning traces)
Rigorous methodology with appropriate controls, multiple metrics, balanced trial selection, and statistical reporting that reduces measurement dependence
Outstanding reproducibility with exceptionally detailed supplementary methods (Appendix C), specific hyperparameters, and clear experimental protocols enabling replication
Excellent presentation with clear writing, effective visualizations (particularly Figure 1), and logical progression from main findings to supporting experiments
Novel findings that confidence representations go beyond token log-probabilities (Section 2.6) and systematic information flow analysis that effectively rules out just-in-time computation
Honest limitations discussion acknowledging that experiments are prompt-specific and don't test sensitivity to paraphrasing or alternative framings
weaknesses: Substantial unexplained variance: variance partitioning analysis reveals R²=0.38, meaning ~62% of verbal confidence variance is unaccounted for by PNML activations, suggesting either distributed encoding or overlooked mechanisms

Partial recovery in critical activation patching experiments (50-70% confidence recovery when PNML is restored) indicates confidence encoding is distributed beyond PNML, undermining claims that PNML is a sufficient cache

Limited mechanistic understanding of the actual computation: while the paper identifies WHERE and WHEN confidence is cached, it provides minimal insight into WHAT operations are performed or what specific aspects of question-answer fit are being evaluated

Incomplete characterization of the distributed confidence mechanism: the paper doesn't systematically identify which other layers/positions contribute to the unexplained 62% of variance or how much they contribute
Attention blocking experiments lack granularity, blocking attention in layer ranges rather than identifying precise critical layers, limiting ability to map sequential information flow precisely

Limited sensitivity testing to prompt variations: all experiments use fixed prompt structures; no testing of robustness to paraphrasing, alternative framings, or person-specific language variations despite this being acknowledged as a limitation

Insufficient exploration of alternative explanations: cross-confidence swap results could reflect redundant encoding rather than true caching, and alternative hypotheses fitting the data are not thoroughly discussed
Limited exploration of failure modes and edge cases: unclear how the cached mechanism behaves with ambiguous questions, out-of-distribution examples, or adversarial settings
Mechanistic vs. correlational distinction: interventions demonstrate correlation (PNML/CC are involved) but strong claims about 'how' computation occurs may overstate causation
Limited practical implications: primarily a mechanistic analysis without clear actionable insights for improving confidence calibration, mitigating overconfidence, or enhancing model reliability
